images.caption: Figure 2:Framework of ZeroVLN.The brain delegates semantic requests to an action expert. Request-grounded supervision first adapts the expert; joint agentic RL then improves both policies without navigation-domain SFT of the brain.

Figure 3:Action Expert Architecture.Semantic queries (NqN_{q}) and visual tokens (NvN_{v}) condition action generation.NfN_{f}flow steps predict anHH-step sequence; only itshh-step prefix is executed before visual replanning.

Figure 4:Request Grounding And Reference Trajectory Generation.The trajectory planner maps the original movement request to a scene instance and reachable endpoint. Red curves mark grounding correspondences. Semantic maps and mesh geometry are used only during training.

Figure 6:Navigation Training Mechanisms.SFT fits the brain to prescribed navigation outputs. ZeroVLN instead reinforces its sampled semantic requests through navigation returns, building on the brain’s existing capabilities.
Figure 7:Small Brain Updates and Retained Capabilities.ZeroVLN largely preserves general visual capabilities with substantially smaller VLM weight changes than NaVILA and DualVLN.

Figure 10:Recovery from Blocked Motion in R2R.The brain changes its view and revises blocked climbing requests, reaches the second landing, and stops at round 25, illustrating feedback-driven coordination with the action expert.
Figure 13:Joint Optimization and Rewards under Round-Level Credit.We obtain conclusions consistent with those under trajectory-level credit (Figure12).
Figure 14:Consistency between predicted trajectories and planner goals before and after joint RL, with additional details provided in AppendixE.2.
